subject: Post-incident technical review and verification schedule
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Tan <elaine.tan@morningstar.com>, ops@morningstar.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial investigation summary — April 24 tokenization latency event

Hi Elaine / Morningstar team,

Thank you again for the patience while we investigated last Saturday's tokenization latency spike. This note summarizes what we know so far and the immediate mitigations we applied. I'll follow up with a full RCA and executable remediation timeline by EOD tomorrow.

What happened (high level):
- On 2027-04-24 22:03 UTC we observed a sustained increase in tokenization latency on the model-serving tier for the region handling your requests.
- Root cause (initial triage): transient KV cache eviction in a subset of worker pods combined with a change in sequence-length distribution from several large backfill jobs.

Immediate actions taken by Redwood:
- Rolled out a targeted cache-protection fix to the affected pool (no customer-facing config changes required).
- Increased priority for your traffic to the hot-path routing policy for a 6-hour window to stabilize latency.
- Captured full diagnostic logs and traces; we will share the sanitized artifacts.

Impact: brief degradation for ~45 minutes affecting ~6% of your requests during the window noted above. No data leakage; all requests processed by Redwood runtime only.

Next steps:
- Full RCA to you by 2027-04-27 EOD (PDF + logs).
- Proposed verification window that we can run together the week of 2027-05-03.

If you want an interim call today, Monica and I are available between 11:00–13:00 PT.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Karthik,

Thanks for the update and quick remediation. We appreciate the priority routing. A couple asks so we can brief our platform stakeholders tomorrow:
1) Can you provide an RCA doc that includes a concise timeline (UTC), the specific root cause chain, and the exact mitigations you will deploy to prevent recurrence?
2) We need sanitized logs and the list of model variants that were affected.
3) Please propose two 1-hour windows next week where Redwood can run traffic validation with our engineers.

Also please include any follow-on remediation that may require customer-side testing or config changes.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Tan
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform — Morningstar

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Tan <elaine.tan@morningstar.com>, ops@morningstar.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T17:38:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-incident technical review and verification schedule

Elaine — attached is the full RCA package and a recommended verification plan. Summary below; full PDF attached (morningstar-rca-20270427.pdf).

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-04-24 22:03:12 UTC — 2027-04-24 22:48:37 UTC (45m 25s).
- Primary impact: median tokenization latency increased from ~40ms to ~310ms for a subset of requests; tail latency hit customer SLO for ~45 minutes.
- Root cause (chain): an automated background backfill job increased average sequence lengths for a traffic segment, which increased KV cache pressure; simultaneously an aggressive cache-eviction heuristic in a platform agent triggered premature eviction on ~12% of shards. The eviction created repeated rehydration penalties and thrashing under load.

Technical timeline (key events, UTC):
- 22:03:00 — anomaly alarms triggered for latency per-route.
- 22:04:10 — runtime tracing shows elevated KV miss rate on pool-7 workers.
- 22:09:40 — cache-eviction agent performed compaction on 12% of shard set due to heuristic threshold crossing.
- 22:12:00 — rehydration traffic caused parallel tokenization CPU saturation on 3 workers; latency escalated.
- 22:30:00 — automated mitigation (increase in routing priority) applied for impacted customer routes.
- 22:48:37 — metrics returned to baseline.

What we changed (short-term fixes already deployed):
1) Tuned the eviction heuristic to increase the threshold for compaction under high sequence-length variance.
2) Increased the per-route hot-path routing priority for affected customers during the event and extended the safety window for 90 minutes after stabilization.
3) Added a quick guard to detect simultaneous high miss-rate + compaction and temporarily pause compaction on impacted shards.

Planned medium/long-term mitigations (owned by Redwood):
- Engineering: implement a KV cache hotness predictor to avoid reactive compaction (ETA 6 weeks).
- Runtime: add proactive per-route rate-aware cache reservations to reduce cross-traffic interference (ETA 10 weeks).
- Controls: surface a per-customer sequence-length anomaly alert in the Console (ETA 3 weeks).

Customer actions recommended (minimal):
- If your backfill jobs can be rate-limited during high-traffic hours, that reduces peak sequence-length variance; not required but helpful.
- We will provide a small test script to emulate your recent traffic pattern (no credentials required) so your team can validate in a staging environment — we propose running that together.

Attachments included:
- morningstar-rca-20270427.pdf (full report, includes sanitized traces and graphs)
- kv-eviction-logs-20270424.zip (sanitized log snippets)

Proposed verification windows (PT):
- Option A: Tue 2027-05-03 09:00–10:00 PT
- Option B: Thu 2027-05-05 13:00–14:00 PT

Action items and owners:
- Redwood: Provide sanitized artifact bundle + runbook for verification (Owner: Karthik) — by 2027-04-27 EOD.
- Redwood Eng: Ship eviction-heuristic rollback as a safety patch to the region (Owner: Hannah) — deployed 2027-04-25 03:20 UTC.
- Morningstar: Confirm which verification window you prefer and whether you want Redwood to run the load generation or co-run it with your engineers.

If helpful, we can run a 30-minute technical walkthrough of the PDF before the verification window. Monica, Hannah and I are on the thread for scheduling.

Thanks again for raising this; our priority is to ensure this does not recur.

-Karthik
[Attachment: morningstar-rca-20270427.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]
[Attachment: kv-eviction-logs-20270424.zip (zip, 2.8MB)]

Subject: Re: Post-incident technical review and verification schedule

Karthik / Monica,

Thanks for the thorough RCA and the artifacts — we reviewed the PDF this morning. Morningstar accepts Option A (Tue 2027-05-03 09:00–10:00 PT) for the verification window.

We'd like Redwood to co-run the test with our platform team and provide step-by-step runbook instructions in advance. Please confirm the Zoom link and the list of Redwood participants; we'll invite our infra engineers and a product security PM.

Also a quick question: after the heuristic tuning you applied, do you expect any change in global performance characteristics (e.g., a small increase in memory usage or a different eviction cadence)? If so, please include those expected deltas in the runbook.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Elaine
